subject: Error: Hessian is singular - but I provided starting values and have no covariates!

messages.author: 44c445bae4eebd56
messages.subject: Error: Hessian is singular - but I provided starting values and have no covariates!
parts:
I am attempting to run a very basic occupancy model in unmarked using occu(). I imported three detection matrices (from camtrapR) in identical formats, and ran the same bare-bones model on each data set just to get occupancy and detection probabilities:

model <- occu(~1 ~1, data = grid)

The model ran for two of the three datasets without a problem, but the third gave the error: 

Error: Hessian is singular.  Try providing starting values or using fewer covariates.

I have tried providing starting values by adding "starts = c(0,0)" (and a couple of different values just to test), and there are no covariates. Any other ideas about what might cause this error?

Below is some more info on the data set that is not working. There are a lot more 0 observations—could that be the issue? All three data sets have many NA observations.

Best,
Kaitlyn

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Error: Hessian is singular - but I provided starting values and have no covariates!
parts:
Hi Kaitlyn,

the issue with that dataset is that the species was detected at all sits which means occupancy is 1. In this case the model can't estimate parameters and there really is no need for an occupancy model. If I interpret your summary right the number of observations are really large indicating that in some cases you had almost 1000 sampling occasions. Even with camera traps and a one-day sampling period that would require over 2.5 years of sampling which would certainly violate any closure assumption. In any case you might want to reduce your sampling periods to 5 or 7 days.

Deepening on your dataset and research questions you might also want to analyze the three datasets in a single model with some parameters shared.

Best,

Mathias
